features.name: Array text conversion
features.description: Ordinary array joining and text conversion execute independently in JS and collecting zero-import WASM, with the selected cycle error and original evaluation order.

scenarios.given: an empty array and a sparse four-position array
scenarios.when: both arrays are joined with default separators
scenarios.then: empty text and exactly three separators are returned

scenarios.given: negative zero, NaN, infinity, the smallest subnormal and Unicode text
scenarios.when: the values are joined with a vertical bar
scenarios.then: their exact existing JS text is retained

scenarios.given: two positions refer to the same noncircular child
scenarios.when: the parent is joined
scenarios.then: both child occurrences are preserved

scenarios.given: separator conversion appends an array item
scenarios.when: join converts that separator
scenarios.then: the original length is used and the append remains observable
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let* ((a (js-array "x")) (sep (js-object :toString (lambda () (js-call a :push "late") "|")))) (let ((out (js-call a :join sep))) (js-array out (js-length a)))))

scenarios.given: the first element conversion changes the second element
scenarios.when: join reads elements in order
scenarios.then: the later read observes the changed value

scenarios.given: toString returns an object and valueOf returns a number
scenarios.when: the containing array is joined
scenarios.then: callbacks run once in string-hint order and the number becomes text
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let* ((trace (js-array)) (item (js-object :toString (lambda () (js-call trace :push "to") (js-object)) :valueOf (lambda () (js-call trace :push "value") 7))) (out (js-call (js-array item) :join))) (js-array out (js-call trace :join ">"))))

scenarios.given: an own join function is replaced while evaluating an argument
scenarios.when: the original method call completes
scenarios.then: the previously captured function is called

scenarios.given: toString has an ignored argument that installs an own join
scenarios.when: toString executes after the argument
scenarios.then: the newly installed join is observed

scenarios.given: an own join returns a source object
scenarios.when: array toString calls that join
scenarios.then: the exact original object is returned

scenarios.given: an array item points to the containing array
scenarios.when: join is attempted and the item is then replaced
scenarios.then: both targets report ELI-RT0009 and the same array can be joined afterwards
scenarios.source: (defvar values (js-array "苹果" nil "香蕉")) (defun run () (put values 1 values) (js-call values :join "、")) (defun recover () (put values 1 "梨") (js-call values :join "、"))

scenarios.given: two arrays refer back to each other
scenarios.when: array toString is attempted and the first edge is replaced
scenarios.then: both targets report the cycle error and release the active conversion state
scenarios.source: (defvar values (js-array nil)) (defvar other (js-array values)) (defun run () (put values 0 other) (js-call values :toString)) (defun recover () (put values 0 "safe") (js-call values :toString))

features.name: Represented type and null queries
features.description: Type queries inspect represented bindings without string conversion, retain lexical capture and member failure, and keep the current four null-predicate meanings. Unsupported capabilities remain explicit.

scenarios.given: values include nil, undefined, Boolean, Number, String, Array and a function
scenarios.when: typeof queries run inside the compiled module
scenarios.then: the exact seven JS labels are returned
scenarios.source: (defun label (value) (js* "typeof value")) (defun run () (js-array (label nil) (label undefined) (label false) (label -0.0) (label "中😀") (label (js-array)) (label label)))

scenarios.given: a closure captures an object whose member is later changed
scenarios.when: the captured member type is queried
scenarios.then: the later undefined value is observed

scenarios.given: a represented object has no requested member
scenarios.when: its member type is queried
scenarios.then: undefined is returned without stringifying the object

scenarios.given: the operand is undefined and one expression counts its own evaluation
scenarios.when: nil, undefined and null predicates are applied
scenarios.then: their existing meanings remain distinct and the effect runs once
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((value undefined) (trace (js-object :calls 0))) (js-array (nil? value) (undefined? value) (null value) (nullish? value) (null (progn (put trace :calls (1+ (get trace :calls))) value)) (get trace :calls))))

scenarios.given: the operand is nil
scenarios.when: all four null predicates are applied
scenarios.then: nil is not confused with undefined

scenarios.given: the represented receiver is nil
scenarios.when: a member type is queried
scenarios.then: member access fails instead of being mislabeled undefined

scenarios.given: raw JS refers to an unrepresented ambient name
scenarios.when: the module is compiled for managed WASM
scenarios.then: source-bound ELI-B0001 refuses the unsupported capability

scenarios.given: an array contains an object with an own dotted property name
scenarios.when: numeric, quoted and negative zero member paths are queried
scenarios.then: all three paths report the exact value type

scenarios.given: a closure captures an array whose element changes
scenarios.when: the closure queries the new element through its captured binding
scenarios.then: the changed Boolean type is observed

scenarios.given: an empty array has no first element
scenarios.when: a query accesses a member of that missing element
scenarios.then: the intermediate access fails instead of returning undefined

scenarios.given: a valid JS query uses a computed member key
scenarios.when: the current experimental managed target compiles it
scenarios.then: the unsupported computed key is explicitly refused

scenarios.given: an operand counts its own evaluation and returns undefined
scenarios.when: the existing value-type intrinsic queries it
scenarios.then: undefined is returned and the count is one

scenarios.given: objects contain an own language brand or inherit it from a prototype
scenarios.when: value-type and raw typeof inspect them
scenarios.then: only own recognized data brands affect value-type and raw typeof stays object
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let* ((value (js-object :kind "eliscript/keyword")) (child (js-object))) (put child :__proto__ value) (js-array (value-type nil) (value-type value) (js* "typeof value") (value-type child))))

features.name: Text formatting and decomposition
features.description: Pure WASM mappings, exact numeric text, UTF16 padding, replacement and splitting retain source conversions and failures

scenarios.given: mixed scripts, a contextual sigma and a lone UTF16 surrogate
scenarios.when: upper and lower casing run
scenarios.then: full Unicode mappings preserve expansion, context and lone code units

scenarios.given: astral fillers and fractional target lengths
scenarios.when: start and end padding run
scenarios.then: padding truncates by UTF16 code unit and converts the target length

scenarios.given: an exact fractional Number and radix 16
scenarios.when: the Number is converted then cased and padded
scenarios.then: the full ordinary method chain yields the exact text

scenarios.given: two matches and a callback using offsets and the original string
scenarios.when: every match is replaced
scenarios.then: both callbacks receive original UTF16 offsets and input
scenarios.source: (defun run () (js-call "a😀a" :replaceAll "a" (lambda (match index original) (str match ":" index ":" original))))

scenarios.given: effectful numeric and separator conversion hooks with a zero limit
scenarios.when: literal split runs
scenarios.then: numeric conversion precedes text conversion even for an empty result
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let* ((trace (js-array)) (n (js-object :valueOf (lambda () (js-call trace :push "limit") 0))) (s (js-object :toString (lambda () (js-call trace :push "separator") "/")))) (js-array (js-call "a/b" :split s n) (js-call trace :join ">"))))

scenarios.given: a separator with an optional capture
scenarios.when: the capture does not participate in a split match
scenarios.then: undefined is an owned element and is distinct from a hole

scenarios.given: a radix below two and a subsequent valid conversion
scenarios.when: Number.toString validates its radix
scenarios.then: a RangeError is raised without contaminating later calls
